overview: American International Group is a global property-casualty (general) insurer providing commercial and personal insurance products to corporate, institutional, and individual customers in over 190 countries. Following the multi-year divestiture and full deconsolidation of its former Life and Retirement business (Corebridge Financial, fully exited May 2026) and the 2023 sale of Validus Re to RenaissanceRe, AIG is now a pure-play general insurer organized into three segments: North America Commercial, International Commercial, and Global Personal. The company is headquartered in New York and completed a leadership transition in 2026, with former Aon executive Eric Andersen succeeding long-time turnaround CEO Peter Zaffino (who moved to Executive Chair before departing for Palantir).

business_model.summary: AIG earns revenue primarily from net premiums earned on property-casualty and specialty insurance policies, plus net investment income on its general-insurance investment portfolio. Underwriting income (premiums less losses and expenses) is the primary profit driver, supplemented by investment returns on float. With Corebridge fully divested, AIG no longer earns spread-based life/annuity income; it is now a focused general insurer with underwriting discipline (combined ratio) as the central value driver, augmented by substantial capital return (buybacks/dividends) funded by divestiture proceeds and underwriting profit.

revenue_streams.name: North America Commercial (property, casualty, financial lines, specialty)
International Commercial (EMEA, UK, Japan, APAC, Latin America, Talbot/Lloyd's, Global Specialty)
Global Personal (Accident & Health, Personal Lines including high-net-worth)

business_model.customer_type: Predominantly B2B/institutional — large corporate, multinational, and mid-market commercial clients (property, casualty, financial lines) — plus a smaller book of individual/personal lines (high-net-worth homeowners, personal accident, travel, warranty products)
business_model.geographic_mix: Global operations across North America, EMEA, UK, Japan, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and China; broadly diversified with North America Commercial as the single largest segment

competitive_position.market_position: Top-tier global commercial P&C insurer with leading positions in large corporate/multinational risk, financial lines, and specialty (including Lloyd's platform Talbot); one of the largest U.S. commercial lines writers by premium alongside Chubb and Travelers, though it trails Chubb in overall U.S. commercial market share

moat_factors.description: Decades of global claims and loss data across complex commercial risks support sophisticated risk selection and pricing that smaller carriers cannot replicate
Ability to service large multinational corporate clients across 190+ countries with locally admitted paper is a significant barrier for regional competitors

One of the oldest and best-known global insurance brands, with deep broker and corporate relationships, though brand was damaged by the 2008 financial crisis bailout and has required a multi-year rebuild
Investment-grade ratings and a de-risked, simplified balance sheet post-Corebridge/Validus support competitive capacity in large-limit and catastrophe-exposed lines
Access to the Lloyd's market broadens specialty and excess/surplus lines capabilities difficult for standard-lines-only competitors to match

weaknesses: Historically higher expense ratio than best-in-class peers (Chubb), though management is targeting <30% General Insurance expense ratio by 2027
Long tail of legacy reserve risk from decades of prior-year commercial and casualty business, particularly long-tail casualty lines
Smaller and less diversified than Chubb or Travelers following the Corebridge/Validus divestitures, with fewer offsetting revenue streams
Exposure to a highly competitive, increasingly soft property/specialty pricing cycle after several years of hard-market rate gains
Leadership transition risk with a new external CEO (Andersen) replacing the architect of the recent turnaround

growth_drivers: Continued underwriting margin improvement toward Investor Day targets (General Insurance expense ratio <30% and Global Personal combined ratio ~94% by 2027)
Selective, profitable premium growth in North America Commercial, International Commercial, and Global Specialty, particularly excluding softening North America property pricing

Capital deployment into buybacks and a growing dividend (11% increase declared in Q1 2026, fourth consecutive year of double-digit dividend growth) now that Corebridge/Validus proceeds have been redeployed
Operating EPS growth target of >20% CAGR over the three years ending 2027, driven by margin expansion, buybacks, and reduced share count
AI and technology-enabled underwriting/claims modernization initiatives to improve loss ratios and expense efficiency
New CEO Eric Andersen's broker/distribution expertise (ex-Aon) potentially deepening broker relationships and driving further organic growth
Further international expansion in Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and specialty/E&S lines where AIG has historically been under-penetrated relative to Chubb

business.risk: Reserve adequacy on long-tail casualty lines
business.description: AIG has a multi-decade history of adverse reserve development on excess casualty and other long-tail commercial lines; continued adequacy is a key watch item for investors and rating agencies

After several years of hard-market rate increases, increased capacity and competition (from Travelers, Zurich, Chubb, Allianz, AXA XL and new entrants) are pressuring rates in property and some specialty lines

New CEO Eric Andersen (external hire from Aon, effective mid-2026) must sustain the underwriting discipline and cultural turnaround delivered by predecessor Peter Zaffino, who has since departed for Palantir
With Life & Retirement (Corebridge) and reinsurance (Validus Re) both fully divested, AIG's earnings are now more concentrated in general insurance underwriting cycles versus more diversified peers

financial.description: Property, specialty, and personal lines remain exposed to hurricanes, wildfires (e.g., 2025 California wildfires), and other natural catastrophes that can cause large quarterly earnings volatility despite reinsurance protection
Net investment income on the general insurance float is sensitive to interest rate moves and credit spreads; a rate-cutting cycle could compress reinvestment yields
Substantial International Commercial and Global Personal premiums are written in non-USD currencies, creating translation risk on reported results

regulatory.description: AIG is subject to state insurance regulation in the U.S. (NAIC risk-based capital), plus international regulatory regimes (Lloyd's/PRA in the UK, Solvency II-equivalent regimes in EMEA, and local regulators across Asia) governing capital, reserving, and conduct

As one of the largest and oldest global insurers, AIG faces ongoing litigation, regulatory inquiries, and legacy exposure (e.g., asbestos/environmental, historical AIG Financial Products-related matters) though these have diminished significantly since the financial crisis era

macro.description: A slowdown could reduce commercial exposure bases (payrolls, revenues, insured values) that drive premium growth, and pressure loss-cost inflation dynamics
Rising jury verdicts, nuclear verdicts, and litigation funding continue to pressure casualty loss costs across the industry, a persistent macro/legal trend affecting long-tail reserves
Secular increase in frequency and severity of wildfires, hurricanes, and severe convective storms raises long-term catastrophe loss-cost trends across the property and specialty book

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global commercial insurance market (~$1.56T in 2026, growing at ~5.9% CAGR through 2031) remains attractive but is transitioning from a multi-year hard market into a more competitive, moderating-rate environment, especially in property; casualty lines continue to see loss-cost pressure from social inflation
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — commercial insurance premium volume is tied to economic activity (payrolls, trade, industrial output) and pricing is cyclical (hard/soft market), but demand for coverage is relatively non-discretionary
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — net investment income on AIG's large fixed-income portfolio benefits from higher-for-longer rates; a rate-cutting cycle would gradually compress reinvestment yields on the float
key_input_costs: Loss cost trends (medical inflation, construction/materials costs, social inflation/litigation)

recent_developments.event: Reported adjusted after-tax EPS of $2.00 (+10% YoY), beating consensus of $1.94; underwriting income of $686M (+10% YoY); accident-year combined ratio (as adjusted) improved 30bps to 88.1%; net premiums written +9% (+11% ex-North America property); returned $904M to shareholders ($641M buybacks, $263M dividends)

CEO transition completed: Eric Andersen (former Aon president) formally became President and CEO after June 1, 2026; predecessor Peter Zaffino moved to Executive Chair and subsequently announced departure from the AIG board (effective Sept 15, 2026) to become global head of financial services at Palantir Technologies

Reported 'excellent' Q1 2026 results with underwriting income more than tripling YoY on lower catastrophe losses (California wildfires markedly lower than the prior-year period); North America Commercial NPW +36% YoY, International Commercial +12%, Global Personal +11% (constant dollar)

AIG completed the sale of its remaining ~5.6% stake in Corebridge Financial for ~$710M net proceeds, fully exiting the Life & Retirement business it began separating in 2021 (following a Feb 2026 buyback of 24.7M Corebridge shares by Corebridge itself for $750M)
Board declared an 11% increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.50/share, the fourth consecutive year of double-digit dividend growth, alongside continued large share repurchases

Delivered $7.09 adjusted after-tax EPS for FY2025, which management noted fully replaced the earnings contribution previously provided by the now-divested Corebridge and Validus Re businesses in under two years; returned $6.8B to shareholders in 2025 via dividends and buybacks
Continued reinvestment in AI-enabled underwriting and claims modernization tools as part of the ongoing operational transformation begun under Zaffino

items.notes: Q2 2026 core operating ROE was 11.1% (11.6% for H1 2026), tracking within the targeted range
Q2 2026 expense ratio was 30.8%, improved 20bps YoY; management reaffirmed the sub-30% target on the Q2 2026 call
Part of the 2024 Investor Day multi-year underwriting improvement targets
Driven by underwriting margin improvement, buybacks, and reduced share count post-Corebridge/Validus divestitures
11% increase declared in Q1 2026 to $0.50/share quarterly, the fourth consecutive year of double-digit growth

items.target: Continued organic growth, moderating in property
items.notes: Management flagged competitive pressure moderating North America property growth while other commercial and specialty lines continue to grow

guidance.management_commentary: Management (new CEO Eric Andersen, alongside CFO) emphasized continued progress toward 2024 Investor Day targets — sub-30% expense ratio, 10-13% core operating ROE, and >20% operating EPS CAGR — underpinned by disciplined underwriting, selective growth in high-performing global commercial and specialty lines, and continued large capital returns to shareholders now that the Corebridge and Validus Re divestitures are complete and proceeds have been substantially returned or redeployed.

bull_case: Now a focused, simplified pure-play general insurer after fully exiting Life & Retirement (Corebridge) and reinsurance (Validus Re), removing complexity and capital drag that previously depressed the valuation multiple

Sustained underwriting margin improvement (accident-year combined ratio 88.1% in Q2 2026, down from years of underperformance) with clear multi-year targets (sub-30% expense ratio, 94% Global Personal combined ratio by 2027)

Substantial and growing capital returns — $6.8B returned in 2025, continued large buybacks and an 11% dividend increase in 2026 — directly supporting EPS growth (>20% CAGR target) and reducing share count
Improved reserve position and five consecutive years (2021-2025) of underwriting profitability under the recent turnaround, reducing (though not eliminating) legacy reserve-adequacy concerns
New CEO Eric Andersen brings deep global broker/distribution relationships from Aon, potentially unlocking further organic premium growth and cross-sell opportunities
bear_case: Loss of Peter Zaffino, the architect of AIG's underwriting turnaround, to Palantir introduces execution and cultural continuity risk under an external, first-time insurance-carrier CEO
Softening commercial property and specialty pricing after a multi-year hard market could pressure premium growth and margins as competition intensifies from Chubb, Travelers, Zurich, and Allianz
AIG's decades-long history of adverse reserve development on long-tail casualty lines means reserve risk, while improved, remains a persistent overhang versus best-in-class peers like Chubb
Now less diversified than before the Corebridge/Validus divestitures, concentrating earnings entirely in general-insurance underwriting and catastrophe cycles
Elevated exposure to climate-driven catastrophe losses (wildfires, hurricanes) and social inflation/litigation trends in casualty lines could create earnings volatility despite reinsurance protection
